newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan to ban lavish weddings.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to ban lavish weddings.

text.p: Lawmakers voted on Thursday to ban lavish wedding feasts, a Pakistani custom which the government says causes hardship for the poor and middle classes.

Families will be allowed to celebrate with a "valima" or wedding meal at home for relatives and house guests. But larger gatherings at hotels, clubs and other places outside the home will be limited to serving hot and cold soft drinks -- without food.
Fireworks, fusillades and street illuminations will also be prohibited.
Wedding restraints have been in force by presidential decree since March as part of Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif's austerity campaign to weather economic troubles.
Some legislators openly doubt that the new law will be strictly observed.

But the Marriages (Prohibition of Wasteful Expenses) Bill, already passed by the National Assembly of lower house, was adopted by the Senate without much opposition. It needs only presidential assent to become law.
Violations, to be investigated by government-named accountability committees and be punished by fines to a maximum of 300,000 rupees ($7,420) and a minimum of 100,000 rupees ($2,474).

The Senate, which is dominated by Sharif's Pakistan Muslim League party and its allies, rejected opposition amendments to allow meals for up to 100 guests and bar surveillance by the accountability committees.
Sharif's adviser on law, justice and parliamentary affairs Khalid Anwar said the law would save the middle and lower classes from hardship caused by wasteful expenditure.
Senator Akram Shah argued, however, that "The wasteful expenditure is always incurred by the wealthy people and you are providing them free hand by allowing in-house valima dinner."
Opposition senator Shafqat Mahmood said "Laws of this kind are never accepted by society" and asked: "So what will happen to this bill at the stage of implementation?"
"If people do not abide by the law and continue to illuminate their houses, display fireworks and hold lavish valima dinners then it will become a bad law," said another Senator.
